A creature you are hidden from can't target you with abilities that don't have the Area keyword, and you have an edge on ability rolls against them. The edge lasts until the end of the turn in which you stop being hidden.

You stop being hidden from a creature if you no longer have cover or concealment from them, or once an ability, an interaction with an enemy, a move without sneaking, or anything else that reveals you resolves. Sneaking is only possible outside of combat.

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-combat-tools.rules.JournalEntry.DSCTrulesJournal.JournalEntryPage.DSCTfullHiding00]{Full rules: Hiding and Sneaking}

A creature you are hidden from can't target you with abilities that don't have the Area keyword, and you have an edge on ability rolls against them. The edge lasts until the end of the turn in which you stop being hidden.

You stop being hidden from a creature if you no longer have cover or concealment from them, or once an ability, an interaction with an enemy, a move without sneaking, or anything else that reveals you resolves.

House rule: becoming hidden also makes you Sneaking, which halves your speed and lets you move while staying hidden. Remove Sneaking to move at full speed, which ends Hidden. Forced movement and teleports still reveal you.

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-combat-tools.rules.JournalEntry.DSCTrulesJournal.JournalEntryPage.DSCTfullHiding00]{Full rules: Hiding and Sneaking}

While you are hidden from another creature, you can sneak, avoiding making too much noise while moving, to remain hidden. While sneaking, your speed is halved. As long as you only move by sneaking and have cover or concealment, you remain hidden.

House rule: your move stops on the first square where somebody you are hidden from would see you. Remove this condition to move at full speed, which ends Hidden.

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-combat-tools.rules.JournalEntry.DSCTrulesJournal.JournalEntryPage.DSCTfullHiding00]{Full rules: Hiding and Sneaking}

While you are hidden from another creature, you can sneak, avoiding the senses of other creatures as you move around them in the open, to remain hidden. While sneaking, your speed is halved. As long as you are sneaking and both begin and end your move in cover or concealment, you remain hidden.

House rule: only where your move ends is checked; anyone you are hidden from who can see you there sees you. Remove this condition to move at full speed, which ends Hidden.

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-combat-tools.rules.JournalEntry.DSCTrulesJournal.JournalEntryPage.DSCTfullHiding00]{Full rules: Hiding and Sneaking}

Strikes against you take a bane, and creatures you have concealment from are creatures you can hide from. Magical concealment comes from invisibility, magical darkness, illusions and the like; some features see through mundane concealment but not magical, or the reverse.

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-combat-tools.rules.JournalEntry.DSCTrulesJournal.JournalEntryPage.DSCTfullConceal0]{Full rules: Concealment}

Strikes against you take a bane, and creatures you have concealment from are creatures you can hide from. Mundane concealment comes from fog, smoke, foliage, natural darkness and similar obscurement; some features see through mundane concealment but not magical, or the reverse.

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-combat-tools.rules.JournalEntry.DSCTrulesJournal.JournalEntryPage.DSCTfullConceal0]{Full rules: Concealment}

Becoming Hidden

You are hidden from a creature when they cannot see or otherwise observe you and do not know where you are. To hide from a creature, you must have cover or concealment from them, and they must not be observing you: a creature is observing you if they were aware of your specific location before you attempted to hide.

During combat, using the Hide maneuver while you have cover or concealment from a creature who isn't observing you hides you from them automatically, unless the Director deems otherwise. Outside of combat, the Director might ask for a Hide test to determine how well hidden you are.

While Hidden

While hidden from a creature, you can't be targeted by their abilities that don't have the Area keyword, and you gain an edge on ability rolls against them. The first benefit ends as soon as you are no longer hidden. The edge lasts until the end of the turn in which you are no longer hidden, so you can leave cover, use an ability against the creature, and still gain the edge as long as you use the ability before the end of that turn.

Losing It

You are no longer hidden from a creature if you don't have cover or concealment from them. If you use an ability, interact with an enemy, move without sneaking, or otherwise make noise or reveal yourself while hidden, you are no longer hidden once the activity that reveals you resolves. A hidden creature who makes a strike resolves the strike first, then is no longer hidden.

Sneaking

By the book, sneaking is possible only outside of combat. While sneaking, your speed is halved, and you make an Agility test using the Sneak skill to remain hidden as you move.

Sneaking in Combat (house rule)

With this Combat Tools setting on, sneaking is allowed during combat. Whenever you become hidden you also gain the Sneaking condition: your speed is halved and you can move while staying hidden. Every square of the move checks cover and concealment along your whole path and stops you on the first square where somebody you are hidden from would see you. Start and end of the move only asks that the move begins and ends in cover or concealment, closer to the book's wording. Remove Sneaking to move at full speed, which ends Hidden. Forced movement and teleports reveal you either way.

Searching

You can look for creatures hidden from you within 10 squares that you have line of effect to. Make an Intuition test using the Search skill; each hidden creature in range makes an Agility test using the Hide skill to oppose it. If your total is higher, they are no longer hidden from you, and you can point them out to allies within 10 squares as part of the same maneuver.

Combat Tools tracks Hidden per creature. Select the hiding token to see who it is hidden from.

Draw Steel: Heroes, Hide and Sneak p. 258 to 259, Sneaking p. 259.

A creature has concealment from you if you can't see or otherwise observe them clearly, even if you have line of effect to them. Strikes against a creature with concealment take a bane, and having concealment from a creature is one of the ways you can hide from them.

Magical concealment comes from magic and supernatural effects: invisibility, magical darkness, illusions and the like. Invisible creatures always have magical concealment.

Mundane concealment comes from the environment: fog, smoke, foliage, natural darkness and similar obscurement.

Some features see through mundane concealment but not magical concealment, or the other way around, which is why Combat Tools tracks the two separately. Having no line of effect to a creature at all also counts as concealment from them for as long as it lasts.

Draw Steel: Heroes, Cover, Concealment and Invisible Creatures p. 276.

To cleanse an effect means to end an effect on a target that is ended at the end of their turn or ended by a saving throw.

Example: rewording the Conduit's Healing Grace maneuver.

Was: "You can end one effect on a target that is ended by a saving throw or that ends at the end of their turn."

Is: "You can cleanse one effect on a target."

Source: Brewery Expanded Glossary
